items.settingsPath: services.msc, and set the service you need back to Manual.
items.name: Remote Registry, Fax, RetailDemo, Parental Controls, and NFC payments
items.desc: Disabled outright.

items.settingsPath: services.msc, find SysMain, and set it back to Automatic.
items.name: SysMain (Superfetch)
items.desc: The SysMain prefetching service, formerly Superfetch.
items.riskNote: Superfetch. Helps on mechanical hard drives, roughly neutral on SSDs, and disabling it can slow first-launch times.

items.settingsPath: services.msc, find Windows Search, set Startup type to Automatic (Delayed Start), and press Start. It takes a while to rebuild the index.
items.name: Windows Search indexing
items.desc: The Windows Search indexing service.
items.riskNote: Disabling the search index makes Start menu search and Outlook search dramatically worse. Rarely worth it.

items.settingsPath: services.msc, find Print Spooler, set Startup type to Automatic, and press Start. Then re-add your printer from Settings > Bluetooth and devices > Printers and scanners.
items.name: Print Spooler
items.desc: The print spooler service.
items.riskNote: The machine will not be able to print at all until this is re-enabled.

items.settingsPath: services.msc, find Windows Biometric Service, set it back to Automatic, then re-enroll in Settings > Accounts > Sign-in options.
items.name: Biometrics service
items.desc: The Windows biometric service behind Hello sign-in.
items.riskNote: Windows Hello fingerprint and face sign-in stop working.

items.settingsPath: services.msc, find Touch Keyboard and Handwriting Panel Service, and set it back to Manual.
items.name: Tablet input and touch keyboard
items.desc: The tablet input and touch keyboard service.
items.riskNote: The touch keyboard and pen input stop working. Skipped automatically when a digitiser is detected.

items.settingsPath: Turn Windows features on or off, and tick the feature you need.
items.name: Legacy optional features
items.desc: Steps Recorder, Math Recognizer, Windows Fax and Scan, XPS Writer, and the legacy Media Player.

items.settingsPath: Task Scheduler, or undo the run to re-enable the tasks.
items.name: Telemetry and marketing scheduled tasks
items.desc: Windows Update, Defender, and disk maintenance tasks are explicitly left alone.

items.settingsPath: Settings > Apps > Default apps, choose your browser, and press Set default. This option only opened that page, so there is nothing to undo.
items.name: Change default browser
items.desc: Hands every association the current browser holds to one you already have instead of Edge - not just http and https, but the file types that open in a browser too: .htm, .html, .pdf, .svg and whatever else it has claimed. Removing Edge does this on its own, first - this is for handing them over without removing anything.
items.riskNote: Windows 11 will not let any third-party tool set this silently: the keys are guarded by a kernel driver and a signature Microsoft does not publish. So this reads which browser you have, opens Default apps at it, and tells you the one button left to press. It reports Blocked rather than claiming a success it cannot deliver.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run to go back to the short Windows 11 menu.
items.name: Restore the full right-click menu
items.desc: Brings back the Windows 10 context menu instead of Show more options.

items.settingsPath: Settings > Personalization > Taskbar, and turn the buttons back on.
items.name: Taskbar cleanup
items.desc: Hides Task View, Widgets, Chat, and the search box entirely. Alignment is left as you have it, and Start still searches when you type.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run.
items.name: Verbose sign-in and shutdown messages
items.desc: Replaces the spinner with what Windows is actually doing at sign-in, sign-out, and shutdown.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run.
items.name: Num Lock on at startup
items.desc: Turns Num Lock on at the sign-in screen and for every account.

items.settingsPath: Settings > Privacy and security, or undo the run.
items.name: Settings home page
items.desc: Hides the recommendation-filled Home page so Settings opens on System instead.

items.settingsPath: Settings > Personalization > Start, and turn the recommendations back on.
items.name: Start menu Recommended section
items.desc: Hides the recently-added, recently-opened, and suggested entries under the pinned apps.
items.riskNote: The Recommended block is hidden rather than emptied, so Start becomes pinned apps only. On Home editions Windows sometimes ignores the policy and puts it back at the next feature update.

items.settingsPath: Settings > Accessibility > Keyboard, and turn the Sticky keys shortcut back on.
items.name: Sticky Keys shortcut
items.desc: Stops five taps on Shift opening the Sticky Keys prompt. The feature stays available in Accessibility settings.

items.name: Battery percentage in the system tray
items.desc: Shows the number next to the battery icon instead of only the fill level.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run.
items.name: Skip the lock screen
items.desc: Goes straight to the sign-in prompt instead of the picture you have to dismiss first.

items.settingsPath: Settings > System > Multitasking, and turn Snap windows back on.
items.name: Window snapping
items.desc: Turns off snapping a window by dragging it to an edge, along with Snap Assist and the snap layout flyout.
items.riskNote: Win+arrow and dragging to an edge stop tiling windows. This is muscle memory for a lot of people - it is at Extreme rather than lower for that reason, and it is one to untick if you use it.

items.settingsPath: Settings > Personalization > Taskbar > Taskbar behaviors, and untick Automatically hide the taskbar.
items.name: Auto-hide the taskbar
items.desc: The taskbar slides out of the way and comes back when you move the pointer to that edge.

items.settingsPath: File Explorer > View > Show, and untick File name extensions.
items.name: Show file extensions

items.settingsPath: File Explorer > View > Options, and set Open File Explorer to Home.
items.name: Explorer opens to This PC
items.desc: Instead of Home with its recommended files.

items.settingsPath: File Explorer > View > Show, and untick Hidden items.
items.name: Show hidden files
items.desc: Shows hidden and system files in File Explorer.
items.riskNote: Shows hidden and system files everywhere. Harmless, but it clutters File Explorer.

items.settingsPath: Settings > Bluetooth and devices > Mouse > Additional mouse settings > Pointer Options, and tick Enhance pointer precision.
items.name: Turn off mouse acceleration
items.desc: Clears Enhance pointer precision, so the same physical movement always moves the pointer the same distance. Takes effect at the next sign-in.

items.settingsPath: Settings > System > For developers, and turn End Task off.
items.name: End task in taskbar right-click

items.settingsPath: Undo the run.
items.name: Edge nag suppression
items.desc: Stops desktop shortcut recreation, default-browser prompts, and the first-run experience.

items.settingsPath: Control Panel > Power Options, and choose the plan you want.
items.name: Set an appropriate power plan
items.desc: High Performance on desktops, Balanced on laptops.
items.riskNote: Changes the active power plan. On a laptop this is left on Balanced deliberately, because High Performance pins clocks, and destroys battery life.

items.settingsPath: Control Panel > Power Options > Choose what the power buttons do > Change settings that are currently unavailable, and tick Turn on fast startup.
items.name: Disable Fast Startup
items.desc: Makes shutdown a real shutdown instead of a partial hibernate.
items.riskNote: Boots slower, because Windows can no longer resume the kernel from disk. Worth it on dual-boot machines, where fast startup leaves the Windows filesystem in a state Linux can corrupt, and for clearing stale driver state between restarts.

items.settingsPath: Run powercfg /hibernate on from an administrator command prompt.
items.name: Disable hibernation
items.desc: Turns off hibernation and deletes hiberfil.sys.
items.riskNote: Reclaims disk equal to your RAM, but removes sleep-to-disk, and hybrid sleep. Skipped automatically on battery-powered hardware.

items.settingsPath: Run DISM /Online /Set-ReservedStorageState /State:Enabled from an administrator prompt.
symptoms: not enough disk space for update
items.name: Disable Reserved Storage
items.desc: Releases the disk space Windows reserves for updates.
items.riskNote: Frees roughly 7 GB, but Windows then has to find that space itself at the next feature update, which can fail on a full disk.

items.settingsPath: Settings > Apps > Startup, or Task Manager > Startup apps, and turn the entry back on.
items.name: Disable startup entries
items.desc: Disables every app set to run at login except system dependencies.
items.riskNote: Disables every login item that is not a system dependency. Audio, input, security, and vendor hardware tools are kept.

items.settingsPath: Nothing to restore automatically - re-create the shortcuts you want. The programs themselves were not removed.
items.name: Remove desktop shortcuts
items.desc: Clears every shortcut off the desktop, yours included. Apps stay installed and in Start.
items.riskNote: Every .lnk and .url on your desktop and the shared public desktop goes, shortcuts you made yourself included. Files and folders on the desktop are untouched, folders of shortcuts are left alone, and nothing is uninstalled - every app is still in Start. The links go to the Recycle Bin, so putting one back is a drag out of the bin.

items.settingsPath: Anything it removed went to the Recycle Bin. Restore it from there, or undo the run.
items.name: Clear folders the uninstallers left behind
items.desc: After the vendor uninstallers have run, sends any install folder they left behind to the Recycle Bin.
items.riskNote: Only touches the folder a program itself declared as its install location, and only when the uninstaller left it there. It goes to the Recycle Bin rather than being deleted, so it can be put back - but settings, license files, and saved data stored inside a program's own folder go with it.

items.settingsPath: Nothing can be restored. Updates installed after the run can still be uninstalled.
items.name: Reclaim space from superseded Windows updates
items.desc: Compacts the component store and clears the temp folders. Usually the largest single space win on the list - typically 3-8 GB.
items.riskNote: Opt-in because it is not reversible in the way the rest of this list is: it throws away the backups Windows keeps for uninstalling updates, so afterwards no installed update can be rolled back. If a Windows update breaks something for you, that route is gone. It also takes several minutes and cannot be interrupted safely.

items.settingsPath: Anything it removed went to the Recycle Bin. Restore it from there, or undo the run.
items.name: Hunt for wider leftovers and remove them
items.desc: Searches AppData, ProgramData, Program Files, and the registry for anything named after a program this run uninstalled, and clears what it finds. Folders go to the Recycle Bin and registry keys are backed up first, so the rollback script puts every one of them back.
items.riskNote: A name match is a guess, not proof of ownership, so this can take something belonging to software you are keeping. It only ever matches names of programs this same run uninstalled, it never touches a folder that still holds a running executable, and every path it takes is listed in the log and reversed by the rollback script. If that is not a trade you want, leave it unticked and the narrower sweep above still clears the folders the uninstallers declared.
